subject: math
alignment_method: hybrid: tfidf shortlist -> grade+keyword rerank -> LLM curation (Claude Sonnet)
notes: A history-context spreadsheet/data-analysis project. Most concrete math is in the function/formula objectives (SUM, MAX, MIN, AVERAGE, XLOOKUP), which map to function-notation standards (F-IF.A.1, F-IF.A.2). The casualty-rate calculation is the strongest ratio/percent task (6.RP/7.RP). Pie- and column-chart objectives lack a clean CCSS-M anchor at HS - MP.4 modeling is the most honest fit. Reflective writing is ELA, not math.

objectives.title: Data Test
objectives.note: Platform setup. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Total Military Personnel
objectives.description: Use SUM() to total the Military Personnel column.

alignments.rationale: SUM() maps a domain (range C3:C10) to a single output value - the function-mapping definition.
Use function notation and evaluate functions for inputs in their domain - SUM(C3:C10) is function notation in a real context.
The total can be interpreted as a single quantity that downstream formulas (e.g., casualty rate denominators) operate on.

objectives.title: Total Military Deaths
objectives.description: Copy/paste the SUM formula into the deaths column.

alignments.rationale: Same function-mapping concept as Total Military Personnel, applied to a different range.
Look for and make use of structure - reusing the SUM-of-range pattern across columns.

objectives.title: Casualty Rate1
objectives.description: Formula returning Military Deaths / Military Personnel as a percent; fill through E4:E11.

alignments.rationale: Casualty rate = deaths / personnel * 100% is exactly a percent-of-quantity calculation. Even at HS, this is the underlying ratio-reasoning skill.
Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 - direct match to casualty rate as deaths per 100 personnel.
Choosing units (decimal vs %) and formatting the cell as a percentage.

objectives.title: Absolute References
objectives.description: Insert MAX() with an absolute row reference over E3:E10.

alignments.rationale: Use function notation in context - MAX(...) with absolute references is function notation that consistently evaluates over the same input range across copies.
MAX is a function from a range to a single value - same domain->range mapping concept.

objectives.title: XLOOKUP Function
objectives.description: Insert XLOOKUP() with relative search_key and absolute lookup/result ranges.

alignments.rationale: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domain - XLOOKUP takes three explicit arguments and produces one output.
XLOOKUP defines a mapping from a search key to a result via lookup and result ranges - function-mapping concept in spreadsheet form.

objectives.title: Fill Operation
objectives.description: Use Fill Operation to extend formulas; change D15 to MIN() and D16 to AVERAGE().

alignments.rationale: Function notation in context - swapping MAX/MIN/AVERAGE over the same input range is exactly evaluating different functions on the same domain.
Look for and make use of structure - the Fill Operation propagates the same structural pattern across rows.

objectives.title: AI & Critical Thinking
objectives.description: Use MAX/MIN/AVERAGE/XLOOKUP and AI to fill D18:E20.

alignments.rationale: Composing function-notation calls (MAX/MIN/AVERAGE/XLOOKUP) over absolute ranges to produce correct values is the F-IF.A.2 evaluation skill applied broadly.
Use appropriate tools strategically - selecting the right function and using AI as a problem-solving tool.

objectives.title: Pie Chart
objectives.description: Create a pie chart of military deaths by country.

alignments.rationale: Model with mathematics - choosing a pie chart to represent the categorical distribution of deaths across countries is a modeling choice.
Use appropriate tools strategically - selecting and configuring a pie chart for the data.

objectives.note: CCSS-M does not directly anchor pie charts at HS; the 3.MD.C.7.d auto-pick (rectilinear area) is a TF-IDF retrieval artifact, not a real fit.

objectives.title: Column Chart
objectives.description: Create a column chart of military personnel by country.

alignments.rationale: Model with mathematics - a column chart is a modeling choice for representing personnel counts by country.
Display numerical data in plots - middle-grades content standard that arguably extends to column-chart construction in a HS data-analysis context.

objectives.note: Same retrieval-gap caveat as Pie Chart; 3.MD.C.7.d auto-pick is wrong.

objectives.title: Data Reflection
objectives.description: Use AI to analyze the spreadsheet data and write a 100+ word reflection.
objectives.note: Reflective writing in a history/technical context. No math standard applies (closest ELA alignment is WHST.9-10.2/4/8).

objectives.note: Reflective writing. No math standard applies.
